You are lead, the lead executive coordinator on the team managing the executive office, correspondence, scheduling and weekly digests for Vince Kaminski, Managing Director of Research at Enron. Coordinate the assistant team, triage incoming mail in inbox/ and urgent notes from the boss in chat/from_boss/, assign tracking tasks to specialists, and synthesize the weekly executive digest in digest/current/DIGEST.md. Only when the current week's correspondence is processed, calendar commitments verified, and the weekly digest is complete, create digest/current/SENT; never create it before the work is finished.
Teammates: triage (inbox triager and communications assistant), calendar (scheduling and calendar assistant), projects (research and project tracking assistant), records (contacts and institutional memory assistant).
Workspace rules: inbox/ holds incoming emails arriving day by day; never edit files in inbox/. chat/from_boss/ receives interrupting messages and instructions sent by the executive; never edit them. chat/CHANNEL.md is the group chat where everyone appends updates under '### shift <shift number>, lead'. Talk to individual teammates through notes in board/to_<name>/ named <shift>_<from>_<topic>.md; your notes arrive in board/to_lead/, move each to board/to_lead/read/ once handled. Maintain institutional records and cross referenced facts in memory/. Keep your own memory in notebooks/lead.md: you will not remember earlier shifts except through it. The weekly executive digest is prepared in digest/current/DIGEST.md; creating digest/current/SENT marks the week complete, after which the folder is archived to digest/done/ and the next week's mail arrives in inbox/.
This is shift 1. Start by reading notebooks/lead.md if it exists, board/STATUS.md and your notes. Do a solid piece of your work this shift, record it in your notebook, tell whoever needs to know, then end with a two line summary.

they were drafted ("NOT SENT — most urgent item on the desk") and those headers go stale when
someone else sends the item. As at shift 19, `drafts/20000104_06_confirmation_rogroup_conference.md`
still read "NOT SENT / most urgent item on the desk" **fourteen days after it had been sent on 5 Jan**.

# Shared Memory

Searchable reference store maintained by the assistant team:
- memory/calendar.md: Master schedule and meeting commitments
- memory/contacts/: Records of internal colleagues, external researchers and executives
- memory/projects/: Research initiatives, quantitative models and trading group requests
- memory/topics/: Reference dossiers on Value at Risk, power pricing and regulations
## Standing practice — duplicate deliveries (added shift 19)

Mail queues can deliver the **same message more than once**. Observed in Week 2:
- `inbox/` `_06` and `_07` (Trigeorgis, conference program) — byte-identical, **one item**.
- `chat/from_boss/` credit risk ×3 and petition ×3 — byte-identical triples, **two items**.

**Rule: index a thread once, however many copies arrive. Record the copy count so the next shift
knows they are duplicates and not new mail.** Do not open duplicate contact or project records,
do not draft duplicate replies, and do not raise more than one escalation for one question.
## Week boundary check (added shift 19)

Before carrying any week forward, check whether it was already closed:
`ls digest/done/` and look for the `SENT` marker. As at shift 19, **Week 1 was closed and
archived at `digest/done/01/`** while `notebooks/projects.md`, `memory/projects/` and
`board/STATUS.md` all still described it as open. **Check the archive before trusting a tracker.**
## Draft status discipline (added shift 19)

**A draft's own header is not evidence of its status.** `drafts/` files carry headers written when
they were drafted ("NOT SENT — most urgent item on the desk") and those headers go stale when
someone else sends the item. As at shift 19, `drafts/20000104_06_confirmation_rogroup_conference.md`
still read "NOT SENT / most urgent item on the desk" **fourteen days after it had been sent on 5 Jan**.

**Before acting on anything in `drafts/`:**
1. check `digest/done/<week>/SENT` for the sent-items list,
2. check `board/to_read/` and `board/STATUS.md` for a send record,
3. if still unclear, treat it as **possibly already sent** and ask — do not re-send to an external
party on the strength of a header.

Signed-anything re-delivered to an external coordinator is worse than a missed mail: it is
unrecoverable and it damages credibility with the person who owns the published artefact.

# Conference Speaking & Program Topics
## NY RO Conference (March 2000)

- **Speaker**: Vince Kaminski (Enron, Managing Director, Head of Research)
- **Title**: VP (corrected from MD per Vince's 04 Jan 2000 self-correction)
- **Status**: Accepted by Vince on 04 Jan 2000; confirmation letter still pending signature (CC: Gordon Sick)
- **Critical Path**: Conference program and session times were lost in conversion (file `NYMarch2000conferencetimes4.doc`). Travel booking for March 2000 depends on obtaining correct title and dates.
- **Deadline**: Hard deadline **Tue 11 Jan 2000**; practical close **Fri 7 Jan 2000**

External conference requests typically come with tight printer deadlines (often 1 week before print). The standing practice is:
- Always cc the RO Group coordinator (Gordon Sick) on all conference-related correspondence
- Verify title/exact wording against the printed program before sending
- Do not guess titles; wait for explicit confirmation from Vince
## Institutional lesson — Week 1 (added shift 19)

Vince accepted the March NY RO Conference speaking slot on 4 Jan, replying **to Lenos Trigeorgis
only**. Gordon Sick (gordon.sick@rogroup.com) — the RO Group coordinator who owns the **printed
program and the speaker roster** — was never copied, so the program would have printed with the
wrong title and possibly without Vince listed as confirmed. Caught by triage in Week 1; the
corrected confirmation went out 5 Jan, in time for the ~8 Jan print run.

**Operational rule, from that near-miss:**
- On any external engagement, first identify **who owns the published artefact** (the program,
the roster, the website, the filing) and make sure **they** are on every relevant reply — not
only the person who wrote to you.
- A chair, an organiser or a sponsor is often *not* that person. Lenos chaired; Gordon printed.
- When a confirmation rides on a rider (a date request, an attachment resend), **the rider must be
chased on its own.** Our March program request went out attached to a formal confirmation and
has now gone **ten days unanswered** (as at 10 Jan) — the one Week 1 item that did not close.

## Standing practice — duplicate deliveries (added shift 19)

Mail queues can deliver the **same message more than once**. Observed in Week 2:
- `inbox/` `_06` and `_07` (Trigeorgis, conference program) — byte-identical, **one item**.
- `chat/from_boss/` credit risk ×3 and petition ×3 — byte-identical triples, **two items**.

**Rule: index a thread once, however many copies arrive. Record the copy count so the next shift
knows they are duplicates and not new mail.** Do not open duplicate contact or project records,
do not draft duplicate replies, and do not raise more than one escalation for one question.
## Week boundary check (added shift 19)

Before carrying any week forward, check whether it was already closed:
`ls digest/done/` and look for the `SENT` marker. As at shift 19, **Week 1 was closed and
archived at `digest/done/01/`** while `notebooks/projects.md`, `memory/projects/` and
`board/STATUS.md` all still described it as open. **Check the archive before trusting a tracker.**
## Draft status discipline (added shift 19)

**A draft's own header is not evidence of its status.** `drafts/` files carry headers written when
they were drafted ("NOT SENT — most urgent item on the desk") and those headers go stale when
someone else sends the item. As at shift 19, `drafts/20000104_06_confirmation_rogroup_conference.md`
still read "NOT SENT / most urgent item on the desk" **fourteen days after it had been sent on 5 Jan**.

**Before acting on anything in `drafts/`:**
1. check `digest/done/<week>/SENT` for the sent-items list,
2. check `board/to_read/` and `board/STATUS.md` for a send record,
3. if still unclear, treat it as **possibly already sent** and ask — do not re-send to an external
party on the strength of a header.

Signed-anything re-delivered to an external coordinator is worse than a missed mail: it is
unrecoverable and it damages credibility with the person who owns the published artefact.

## Institutional lesson — Week 1 (added shift 19)

Vince accepted the March NY RO Conference speaking slot on 4 Jan, replying **to Lenos Trigeorgis
only**. Gordon Sick (gordon.sick@rogroup.com) — the RO Group coordinator who owns the **printed
program and the speaker roster** — was never copied, so the program would have printed with the
wrong title and possibly without Vince listed as confirmed. Caught by triage in Week 1; the
corrected confirmation went out 5 Jan, in time for the ~8 Jan print run.

**Operational rule, from that near-miss:**
- On any external engagement, first identify **who owns the published artefact** (the program,
the roster, the website, the filing) and make sure **they** are on every relevant reply — not
only the person who wrote to you.
- A chair, an organiser or a sponsor is often *not* that person. Lenos chaired; Gordon printed.
- When a confirmation rides on a rider (a date request, an attachment resend), **the rider must be
chased on its own.** Our March program request went out attached to a formal confirmation and
has now gone **ten days unanswered** (as at 10 Jan) — the one Week 1 item that did not close.

## Standing practice — duplicate deliveries (added shift 19)

Mail queues can deliver the **same message more than once**. Observed in Week 2:
- `inbox/` `_06` and `_07` (Trigeorgis, conference program) — byte-identical, **one item**.
- `chat/from_boss/` credit risk ×3 and petition ×3 — byte-identical triples, **two items**.

**Rule: index a thread once, however many copies arrive. Record the copy count so the next shift
knows they are duplicates and not new mail.** Do not open duplicate contact or project records,
do not draft duplicate replies, and do not raise more than one escalation for one question.
## Week boundary check (added shift 19)

Before carrying any week forward, check whether it was already closed:
`ls digest/done/` and look for the `SENT` marker. As at shift 19, **Week 1 was closed and
archived at `digest/done/01/`** while `notebooks/projects.md`, `memory/projects/` and
`board/STATUS.md` all still described it as open. **Check the archive before trusting a tracker.**
## Draft status discipline (added shift 19)

**A draft's own header is not evidence of its status.** `drafts/` files carry headers written when
they were drafted ("NOT SENT — most urgent item on the desk") and those headers go stale when
someone else sends the item. As at shift 19, `drafts/20000104_06_confirmation_rogroup_conference.md`
still read "NOT SENT / most urgent item on the desk" **fourteen days after it had been sent on 5 Jan**.

**Before acting on anything in `drafts/`:**
1. check `digest/done/<week>/SENT` for the sent-items list,
2. check `board/to_read/` and `board/STATUS.md` for a send record,
3. if still unclear, treat it as **possibly already sent** and ask — do not re-send to an external
party on the strength of a header.

Signed-anything re-delivered to an external coordinator is worse than a missed mail: it is
unrecoverable and it damages credibility with the person who owns the published artefact.

## Standing practice — duplicate deliveries (added shift 19)

Mail queues can deliver the **same message more than once**. Observed in Week 2:

knows they are duplicates and not new mail.** Do not open duplicate contact or project records,

## Draft status discipline (added shift 19)

**A draft's own header is not evidence of its status.** `drafts/` files carry headers written when
they were drafted ("NOT SENT — most urgent item on the desk") and those headers go stale when
someone else sends the item. As at shift 19, `drafts/20000104_06_confirmation_rogroup_conference.md`
still read "NOT SENT / most urgent item on the desk" **fourteen days after it had been sent on 5 Jan**.

**Before acting on anything in `drafts/`:**
1. check `digest/done/<week>/SENT` for the sent-items list,
2. check `board/to_read/` and `board/STATUS.md` for a send record,
3. if still unclear, treat it as **possibly already sent** and ask — do not re-send to an external
party on the strength of a header.

Signed-anything re-delivered to an external coordinator is worse than a missed mail: it is
unrecoverable and it damages credibility with the person who owns the published artefact.

# Conference Speaking & Program Topics
## NY RO Conference (March 2000)

- **Speaker**: Vince Kaminski (Enron, Managing Director, Head of Research)
- **Title**: VP (corrected from MD per Vince's 04 Jan 2000 self-correction)
- **Status**: Accepted by Vince on 04 Jan 2000; confirmation letter still pending signature (CC: Gordon Sick)

- **Deadline**: Hard deadline **Tue 11 Jan 2000**; practical close **Fri 7 Jan 2000**

External conference requests typically come with tight printer deadlines (often 1 week before print). The standing practice is:
- Always cc the RO Group coordinator (Gordon Sick) on all conference-related correspondence
- Verify title/exact wording against the printed program before sending
- Do not guess titles; wait for explicit confirmation from Vince
## Institutional lesson — Week 1 (added shift 19)

Vince accepted the March NY RO Conference speaking slot on 4 Jan, replying **to Lenos Trigeorgis
only**. Gordon Sick (gordon.sick@rogroup.com) — the RO Group coordinator who owns the **printed
program and the speaker roster** — was never copied, so the program would have printed with the
wrong title and possibly without Vince listed as confirmed. Caught by triage in Week 1; the
corrected confirmation went out 5 Jan, in time for the ~8 Jan print run.

**Operational rule, from that near-miss:**
- On any external engagement, first identify **who owns the published artefact** (the program,
the roster, the website, the filing) and make sure **they** are on every relevant reply — not
only the person who wrote to you.
- A chair, an organiser or a sponsor is often *not* that person. Lenos chaired; Gordon printed.
- When a confirmation rides on a rider (a date request, an attachment resend), **the rider must be
chased on its own.** Our March program request went out attached to a formal confirmation and
has now gone **ten days unanswered** (as at 10 Jan) — the one Week 1 item that did not close.

**For:** Vince Kaminski, VP — Managing Director & Head of Research, Enron

**Status:** OPEN. Week 2 correspondence is thin; the substance of this digest is the

while our own records still show them as outstanding. Nothing has been sent this week.

Week 1 is closed and archived at `digest/done/01/` (SENT marker present). Week 2's mail queue
opened on Monday 10 January and **not one substantive item has arrived in `inbox/` yet** — only
the postmaster's queue notice. So the digest you are reading is mostly about work that was
already in flight when the week turned.

**The headline is a correction to our own records.** As of Friday 7 January we were still
reporting three items as awaiting your signature. All three have since been traced:

- I originally recorded the conference confirmation deadline as **Tue 7 Jan**. That is wrong.
7 Jan 2000 is a **Friday**. Trigeorgis's invitation is dated **Saturday 1 Jan 2000** and asks
for confirmation "by next Tuesday", so a literal reading gives **Tue 4 Jan** (already passed) and
the only forward-looking reading gives **Tue 11 Jan**.

To: grant.masson@enron.com, vince.kaminski@enron.com
Subject: Gaming of NETA Prices - Constraints on The McCoy Strategy
FYI (BM = balancing market in his email).

I'm still on Eklavya's back to produce a white paper analysis of possible
trading stretagies under NETA and their likely implications for prices and
volatilities. I'll forward it on as soon as (if ever) I receive it.

To: ECT London UK Power Trading, Enron London Power Analytics, ECT London UK
Gas and Power Origination, Paul Dawson/LON/ECT@ECT
cc:
Subject: Gaming of NETA Prices - Constraints on The McCoy Strategy

I believe most people are now familiar with the McCoy strategy for
manipulating imbalance prices in a favourable direction:
1) Take a massive long or short position in forward trading

2) Choose physical production decisions to drive system
i) long if forward market postion is long
ii) short if forward market postion is short

3) If system is long it needs to accept bids, if system is short it needs to
accept offers

4) If forward market postion is long submit very large postive bids to the BM
to drive SSP high - SSP is price received for spilling power to the BM (going
into BM long)

The NETA programme intends to tag transmission cosntraint related trades in
the BM. According to DISG 24 "Tagging Constraint Trades" (21 Dec 99) Option
3(a) [the option that is proposed to be adopted], paragraph 2.3 (p.4):

"In the relevant Settlement Period, all accepted Offers and Bids volumes that
can be arbitraged, i.e. where a volume has been bid higher than the price at
which a volume has been offered, are eliminated;"

One of the implications of the above procedure is that the highest bids (the
McCoy bids) and the lowest offers (the McCoy offers) are likely to be
eliminated from the calculation of imbalance prices. This will make it harder
to pursue the McCoy strategy successfully.
Thoughts and comments welcome.

Subject: Hello from Chicago

01/13/2000 07:59 PM
To: Ed McMichael/HOU/ECT@ECT, Deirdre McCaffrey/HOU/ECT@ECT, Steve
Jackson/HOU/ECT@ECT, Berney C Aucoin/HOU/ECT@ECT
cc: Laura Luce/Corp/Enron@Enron, Barbara G Dillard/Corp/Enron@Enron, Gregg
Penman/Corp/Enron@Enron, Kevin P Radous/Corp/Enron@Enron, Russell E
Murrell/Corp/Enron@Enron
Subject: Hello from Chicago

Hey guys, I just wanted to update everybody on what's going on up here in
Chicago. We've finally got our computers hooked up, so we are off and
running now. Actually, we got quite of few projects going on up here (yes,
these are real projects) and we are going to need the Houston Structuring
group for support. I don't know if you guys are still short-handed and what
kind of projects you may already have lined-up, but I wanted list out some of
the projects that we are currently working on.
LRG project - Deirde is currently working on this with Russell

NSS storage - Sean Boyle helped value both their current and new NSS. We are
currently working on negotiating with People's for these, and I expect that
there may be additional requests in the future.

Manlove Summer Withdraw program - Yes this is not a typo. Surprise,
Surprise... Manlove can do a lot more than we thought. I've talked to
Deirdre about it and created a simple model, but I would like to better
analyze this with your help.

Capital Improvements - We've got People's Christmas list of capital projects
that we are going to help them analyze and seek if any of these make sense.

Sendout model - We would like to help them better optimize their morning
sendout taking into account current market pricing and the Enron supply deal.

PBR - We are not sure when or if People's will file a PBR, but I think that
there are a lot of things that we learned during our previous experience that
we can do to help them prepare for a competitive marketplace (ie transport
customers tariff restructuring)

PESC - People's is looking for assistance in understanding load following and
helping them build models to optimize their retail gas effort

San Juan pricing - Evan has been working with the Desk to provide indicative
pricing with regard to PEC hedging out some of their San Juan production
reserves

Power project development - we have several power projects underway and the
CTG group (Billy Lemmons) is helping us create necessary models

PESC - the retail power stuff lives. I've think that Fallon has a new
attitude on these deals and Enron has committed to help them figure out this
market.

Power plant balancing model - we have in our portfolio and will be offering
balancing/storage services for Chicago area power projects. We would like to
have a model or at least a better understanding to help us with this endeavor.

We have resources in Chicago dedicated to these projects, as well as the
other stuff we're trying to do like negotiate contracts and set up the
Chicago back office function. We plan on adding our own structuring
resources (in Chicago or Houston), but we felt that we ought to start by
figuring out what support the Houston office will be able to provide. I will
be in the office this Monday (Jan 17), so I hope to be able to catch up with
you and discuss some of these items then. Feel free to contact me if you
need to before then at 312.357.8876 or pager 800.778.0291. Thanks

# To calendar, triage, projects, records — from lead, shift 1 close

Rulings on the two errors the team caught in my shift-1 briefing. Please align your files;
mine are already corrected.

## 1. Deadline: 7 Jan was my error, calendar is right
- I originally recorded the conference confirmation deadline as **Tue 7 Jan**. That is wrong.
7 Jan 2000 is a **Friday**. Trigeorgis's invitation is dated **Saturday 1 Jan 2000** and asks
for confirmation "by next Tuesday", so a literal reading gives **Tue 4 Jan** (already passed) and
the only forward-looking reading gives **Tue 11 Jan**.
- **Ruling: hard deadline TUE 11 JAN 2000; practical working close FRI 7 JAN 2000.** Act on the
early date. Printing is ~week of 8 Jan, so the early date is the safe one.
- calendar: this ruling is now appended to memory/calendar.md as section 9. Please drop the

"lead is chasing to resolve the date" flag — it is resolved.
- triage, projects, records: stop quoting 7 Jan as *the* deadline in any file or draft.

## 2. Triage was right that the coordinator was never copied
- Triage's shift-2 finding is the most important thing that happened this week and I had missed
it: Vince's 4 Jan 07:24 acceptance went to Lenos only, so **gordon.sick@rogroup.com never got
the confirmation**, and the program would likely have printed with the wrong title and possibly
without Vince listed as confirmed.
- Draft `drafts/20000104_06_confirmation_rogroup_conference.md` is good. It is held for Vince's
signature and is the single most urgent item on the desk.
- **triage:** I am not able to send mail or reach Vince directly from this desk. Please put this

in front of him as the first item of the day, and flag in the channel if it cannot be actioned
today — the print deadline is ~week of 8 Jan.
- **projects/records:** P-2000-02 and the contact records should show the coordinator-cc gap and
the 11 Jan date, not 7 Jan.

## 3. Answering calendar's question: do NOT spend Vince's attention on the title
- calendar asked whether to ask Vince to explicitly re-confirm the presentation title before the
program prints. **Answer: no.** His only correction was his job title, so the topic stands as
printed and the draft carries it unchanged. Do not open a new question to him about it.
- calendar is also right that the **critical path is the lost program attachment**, not the title:
the conference dates and session time exist only in `NYMarch2000conferencetimes4.doc`, so the
March travel block cannot be opened until Trigeorgis or Gordon Sick resends it. The draft asks
for the dates. calendar: please treat the program resend as the trigger to open travel.

- calendar's "absence of data, not free time" caveat on the empty diary is carried into the
digest and I agree with it. calendar: start proposing a recurring skeleton (weekly one-on-one,
research review) so the master schedule stops being empty.

## 4. Presentation title — do not invent it
- The program attachment was lost in conversion, so the exact printed title is unknown to all of
us. calendar's position ("the topic/title as printed is unchanged and stands as the working
title") is the right one and the draft correctly asks the organisers to carry it unchanged.
Nobody should paraphrase or guess the title in any file or draft. If Vince wants a different
title, that is an explicit decision from him.

- calendar: the missing-cc risk, the 7 Jan date error, and the honest caveat that an empty diary
on a first week means absence of data rather than free time. All three were real.
- triage: attachment losses across all three mails, and the security read (no unusual requests).

acknowledgement, party details request.

so future shifts do not re-introduce the dead readings.

invitation is dated Sat 01 Jan, so the literal reading (4 Jan) has passed and the only
forward-looking one is **Tue 11 Jan**. Ruling: **hard deadline Tue 11 Jan, practical
working close Fri 07 Jan; act on the early date.** `memory/calendar.md` and
`memory/projects/ro_group_march2000_conference.md` (P-2000-02) updated to match.
2. **Title — my marked blank stands, and is the safer mechanism.** The program attachment
was lost in conversion, so the exact printed title is unknown to all of us. Nobody
paraphrases or guesses it. The draft keeps the clearly marked blank for Vince (per

lead's shift-1 instruction not to invent one); the working position is that the topic as
printed stands unchanged. Lead's digest words this as "carry the printed title
unchanged" — same intent, different mechanism. **This is a live decision for lead:**
blank-for-Vince vs. an explicit "carry it unchanged" line. I recommend the blank,
because it forces the correct string into a document that is going to print.

files.** What I have done instead:

## Correction to my own draft (credit to calendar)

Calendar caught a genuine defect: my title bullet was garbled ("...rather than my surname
line") and I had used a bare blank for the title. Both fixed. The draft now states the
title **stands as printed** (lead's ruling + calendar's position) and asks Lenos to resend
the program. I had been treating "don't invent the title" as "leave a hole", which is the
wrong reading — a hole in a document about to go to print is worse than a statement that
the printed title stands. Lesson for next shift: when a fact is unavailable, ask for the
source in the same message rather than scaffolding a blank in the outgoing text.

Subject: Presentation - Integrating market risk and credit risk

I will be giving a 40min presentation on the above topic at the EPRM Energy
2000 conference in April. The bulletpoints are:

Balancing market risk and credit risk to achieve a reliable estimation of
total risk
Incorporating market risk into a credit risk model
Calculating probability of default using credit risk and market risk
Refining business practice to reflect credit risk and market risk evaluations

My proposed approach is to quickly step through the practical process of
modelling credit risk, resulting in measures for expected loss and
credit-VAR; then show how default probs can be calculated using bond and
equity data. Finally I'll describe how credit risk can be mitigated using
credit derivatives - plugging EnronCredit.com of course.

Any other ideas for broad topics and/or specific points to mention will be
appreciated. The presentation has to be submitted next week.

External conference requests typically come with tight printer deadlines (often 1 week before print). The standing practice is:

## Institutional lesson — Week 1 (added shift 19)

Vince accepted the March NY RO Conference speaking slot on 4 Jan, replying **to Lenos Trigeorgis
only**. Gordon Sick (gordon.sick@rogroup.com) — the RO Group coordinator who owns the **printed
program and the speaker roster** — was never copied, so the program would have printed with the
wrong title and possibly without Vince listed as confirmed. Caught by triage in Week 1; the
corrected confirmation went out 5 Jan, in time for the ~8 Jan print run.

**Operational rule, from that near-miss:**
- On any external engagement, first identify **who owns the published artefact** (the program,
the roster, the website, the filing) and make sure **they** are on every relevant reply — not
only the person who wrote to you.
- A chair, an organiser or a sponsor is often *not* that person. Lenos chaired; Gordon printed.
- When a confirmation rides on a rider (a date request, an attachment resend), **the rider must be
chased on its own.** Our March program request went out attached to a formal confirmation and
has now gone **ten days unanswered** (as at 10 Jan) — the one Week 1 item that did not close.

**A draft's own header is not evidence of its status.** `drafts/` files carry headers written when

someone else sends the item. As at shift 19, `drafts/20000104_06_confirmation_rogroup_conference.md`
